sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Every column filter now has its own Cc (case-sensitive), Rx (regular expression) and Ex (exclude) switches, as small chips inside the filter field, left of its ✕. Idle chips stay faint until you hover or focus the field; a switched-on chip always shows, and Ex also puts a red stripe down the field's left edge. This makes filters like "CDs, but no live albums" possible: `CD` in Format plus `live` with Ex in Release.

Each level's switches now apply to that level only: the global Cc/Rx/Ex to the global filter string, a sub-table's to its sub-table filter string, and a column's to that column's text and its 📊 selection. Before, column filters borrowed the global switches on single-table pages and the (usually hidden) sub-table switches on multi-table pages. Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click) on a global or sub-table switch also sets it on every column filter it covers.

Columns narrower than 160 px show one small mode button instead of the three chips (`Aa`, or the initials of what is on, e.g. `R·E`); it opens the same switches in a pop-up, with "Apply these modes to every column in this table". The switch follows the column's width live (auto-resize, dragging a column edge, resizing the window). Below about 155 px the chips would cover the middle of the field, so a click meant for the text could toggle a switch.
The 📊 panel of a column whose Ex is on shows a banner: ticked values are then hidden, while each count still says how many rows have the value.
Clearing a column filter (its ✕, Escape, or any Clear button) also switches its modes off.

New settings (🎨 TABLE FILTER CONFIGURATION): "Cc / Rx / Ex Switches On Every Column Filter" (on by default; off restores the previous borrowing behaviour exactly) and "Column Filter Switches: Compact Below (px)" (160; 0 = always the chips).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Multi-table pages: ticking a sub-table filter's Cc, Rx or Ex box (in the 🔍 panel) now re-runs that sub-table's column filters straight away. Those boxes also govern the column filters, but only the sub-table text used to be re-applied, so e.g. a column filter "^Tun" stayed literal after ticking Rx until the next keystroke. Applying a pinned/recent sub-table history entry, which restores the boxes, takes the same path.

Multi-table pages: a sub-table's status line no longer contradicts itself. It used to label the global query with the sub-table's own Cc (`GLOBAL:(case) "e"` with the global Cc off), never showed the global Ex, and after any re-filter counted the rows before the sub-table filter hid any. Both code paths that write it now share one builder.

Multi-table pages with cover art: the image rows of a CAA/EAA cell highlight a global query with the GLOBAL Cc/Rx again, not the sub-table's. A global regexp such as "Back|Nothing" kept the right rows but was highlighted as literal text whenever the sub-table's Rx was off.

A plain (non-Rx) global filter no longer matches across two cells. "Rest Bruce" (the end of the Release cell and the start of the Artist cell) matched every row, with nothing highlighted, while the same text with Rx on matched none. Plain text is now matched cell by cell, like a regexp; several words inside one cell, including a name and its disambiguation comment, still match.

Filter status lines now show the modifiers that apply to each part and the global query as typed: e.g. `✓ Filtered 52 rows in 70ms [1 COLUMN FILTER ['Release':(ex) "live"]]` when the global Ex inverts a column filter on a single-table page, `'Release':(rx) "^Tun"` when a closed 🔍 panel's Rx governs a column on a multi-table page, and `GLOBAL:"BoDeans"` instead of `GLOBAL:"bodeans"`. Before, column filters were listed without modifiers, so an inverted or regexp column filter looked exactly like a plain one.
Filter status lines name a column by its real name again: a column whose header carries a control glyph was printed with it, e.g. `'▌█Barcode'` instead of `'Barcode'`.
